title: Microsoft Purview DLP: discover and protect data sent to unmanaged cloud apps through Palo Alto Prisma Access
summary: The briefing's rollout dates, opt-in default, licensing and general Purview control paths are supported. Minor corrections should flag the preview qualification on the DLP scenario, cite the service description, avoid implying a guaranteed reporting delay and align the checklist with the controls table.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview network data security is adding a Palo Alto Prisma Access integration.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview network data security now integrates with Palo Alto Prisma Access, extending discovery and protection to network traffic.

claims.claim: New and existing Prisma Access customers can use collection policies to discover sensitive data shared with unmanaged cloud apps.
claims.quote: new and existing Palo Alto Prisma Access customers can configure Microsoft Purview collection and data loss prevention policies to discover and protect sensitive data shared with unmanaged cloud apps

claims.claim: DLP policies can protect sensitive data detected through Prisma Access network traffic once the integration is enabled.
claims.quote: Network traffic inspected by Palo Alto Prisma Access can be evaluated by Microsoft Purview DLP policies once the integration is enabled by an administrator.

claims.claim: The planned Prisma Access integration covers HTTP and HTTPS traffic.
claims.quote: discover and protect sensitive data shared with unmanaged cloud apps via HTTP/HTTPS

claims.claim: The integration uses the same classifiers, sensitive information types and sensitivity labels as other Purview policies.
claims.quote: using the same classifiers, sensitive information types, and sensitivity labels used in other Purview policies.

claims.claim: The roadmap says the integration enriches Data Security Posture Management.
claims.quote: This integration further enriches Purview Data Security Posture Management (DSPM)

claims.claim: The roadmap says the integration enriches Insider Risk Management.
claims.quote: This integration further enriches Purview Data Security Posture Management (DSPM), Insider Risk Management (IRM)

claims.claim: The roadmap describes data security and compliance for AI interactions.
claims.quote: enables data security & compliance for AI interactions, and more.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The integration is admin-opt-in, with no user impact unless administrators enable it and configure policies.
claims.quote: The integration is not enabled by default. Administrators must explicitly enable it before it can be used in policies.

claims.claim: The integration automatically appears in the Purview DLP Security Store during rollout and is enabled there.
claims.quote: The Palo Alto Prisma Access integration will automatically appear in the Purview DLP Security Store as the feature rolls out.

claims.claim: Existing network data security collection and DLP policies apply automatically after enablement.
claims.quote: Existing network data security collection and DLP policies will automatically apply after the integration is enabled.

claims.claim: The affected audience includes Purview organisations, current or prospective Prisma Access customers and administrators managing collection and DLP policies.
claims.quote: Organizations using Microsoft Purview.- Customers using or planning to use Palo Alto Prisma Access.- Microsoft 365 administrators managing Purview collection and DLP policies.

claims.where: summary; Cost and licensing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Purview pay-as-you-go must be enabled and configured for the tenant to use this integration.
claims.quote: Confirm that Purview pay-as-you-go is enabled and configured for your tenant, as it is required to use this integration.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Mixed licensing comprises Purview E5 or equivalent per-seat licences and Purview pay-as-you-go for non-Microsoft SASE integrations.
claims.quote: Network data security with non-Microsoft SASE and secure browser solutions requires: Purview E5 (or equivalent) per-seat licenses and the Microsoft Purview pay-as-you-go billing model.

claims.where: front matter: cost; Cost and licensing; Why it matters; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The pay-as-you-go meter for non-Microsoft integrations is the request, supporting a variable cost rating.
claims.quote: Network data security uses the request as unit of measure for pay-as-you-go billing purposes when using non-Microsoft SASE and secure browser integrations.

claims.claim: A request is each network call from a device or browser to a website or API, excluding responses.
claims.quote: A request is each network call made from a device or browser to a website or API. This definition doesn't include the responses to the requests.

claims.claim: Collection policies need no licence of their own, distinct from the workload licensing described above.
claims.quote: There are no licensing requirements to apply collection policies. Instead, you must be licensed for the workload for which you're creating the policy.
claims.fix: Add the Microsoft Purview service description to sources: https://learn.microsoft.com/office365/servicedescriptions/microsoft-365-service-descriptions/microsoft-365-tenantlevel-services-licensing-guidance/microsoft-purview-service-description. It supports both collection-policy licensing statements in this paragraph.

claims.claim: A collection policy using network data protection requires an Azure subscription link because network-based enforcement is pay-as-you-go.
claims.quote: creating a collection policy with network data protection requires the tenant to be linked to an Azure subscription as a prerequisite, since network-based enforcement is a pay-as-you-go feature.

claims.claim: The Microsoft documentation examined does not state Palo Alto's subscription or licence terms for this integration.
claims.quote: Searched: site:learn.microsoft.com "Palo Alto" "Prisma Access" "Purview". Read dlp-network-data-security-learn, dlp-create-policy-ai-network-data-security and collection-policies-create-deploy-policy; these refer provider setup to the provider and state no Palo Alto SKU.

claims.claim: Integrated network solutions monitor traffic and send data to Purview for classification and policy evaluation.
claims.quote: The integrated solutions monitor network traffic and send the data to Microsoft Purview for classification and policy evaluation.

claims.claim: Communication with Purview is real time when applying DLP protection.
claims.quote: When you apply protections via the use of DLP policies, the communication between the integrated solution and Microsoft Purview is in real time.

claims.claim: Learn describes non-Microsoft integrations as generally available or in preview depending on the integration.
claims.quote: Non-Microsoft SASE and secure browser solutions (general availability or preview, depending on the integration)

claims.claim: The cited Learn pages do not name Prisma Access or provide Prisma-specific Purview setup steps as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: site:learn.microsoft.com "Palo Alto" "Prisma Access" "Purview". Read the cited network overview, DLP scenario and collection-policy setup pages in full; none names Prisma Access. Results concern Entra coexistence, not this Purview integration.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Non-Microsoft integration partners can access and possibly store policy configuration including user identifiers.
claims.quote: If you choose to integrate with non-Microsoft partners, they will be able to access and possibly store some policy configuration, including user identifiers.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The partner's terms, conditions and privacy policy govern its use and storage of that policy data.
claims.quote: Their terms, conditions, and privacy policy will govern the usage and storage of this data.

claims.claim: Inline evaluation covers up to 4 MB for uploadText and downloadText.
claims.quote: Inline evaluation size limits: Microsoft Purview evaluates up to 4 MB of content for uploadText and downloadText

claims.claim: Inline evaluation covers files up to 3 MB for uploadFile and downloadFile.
claims.quote: files up to 3 MB for uploadFile and downloadFile.

claims.claim: Purview network data security policies do not apply to B2B guest users.
claims.quote: Purview network data security policies don't apply to B2B guest users.

claims.claim: Encoded content or dynamically generated endpoints in some unmanaged AI apps can affect enforcement.
claims.quote: Some unmanaged AI apps like ChatGPT, Runway and Meta AI might intermittently send content in encoded form or through dynamically generated endpoints, which can impact policy enforcement.

claims.claim: Policies targeting an unmanaged app can capture consumer and enterprise interactions where the URL is shared.
claims.quote: Policies that target unmanaged apps can capture interactions from both the consumer and enterprise versions of an app when the app's URL is shared across instances

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Network DLP supports Audit only and Block actions, subject to provider support.
claims.quote: Actions - Network data security supports Audit only and Block actions.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: A network DLP Block rule can stop text submission and file upload.
claims.quote: Select Text sent to or shared with cloud or AI apps and File uploaded to or shared with cloud or AI apps. Select Block for both.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Scope; Open questions
claims.claim: Supported activities and actions can differ by integrated solution and should be checked with the provider.
claims.quote: The activities and actions supported may differ depending on integrated solution. Check with your solution provider for details on supported activities.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Initial policy distribution and first data can take up to 24 hours, described as meaning results will not appear immediately.
claims.quote: allow up to 24 hours for your policies to be distributed to the network security solution and for the first data to show up.
claims.fix: Replace 'so a test policy will not show results immediately' with 'so a test policy might not show results immediately'. The source gives an upper allowance, not a guaranteed delay.

claims.claim: Non-Microsoft SASE setup requires completing the integration steps in the provider's documentation.
claims.quote: If you are using a non-Microsoft SASE or secure enterprise browser provider ... Ensure you've completed the integration steps outlined in your provider's documentation.

claims.claim: Policies can target unmanaged cloud apps or adaptive app scopes such as all unmanaged AI apps.
claims.quote: Select + Add cloud apps. Select the Adaptive app scopes tab, then choose All unmanaged AI apps and select Add (1).

claims.claim: Network policies can be scoped to specific users and groups.
claims.quote: Select + Add inclusions. Select Specific users and groups. Search for and select the Finance department group, then select Add.

claims.claim: The general supported activities are text sent, file uploaded, text received and file downloaded.
claims.quote: Text sent to or shared with cloud or AI app. File uploaded to or shared with cloud or AI app. Text received from cloud or AI app. File downloaded from cloud or AI app.

claims.claim: The general network data security integrations classify traffic sent and received over HTTP and HTTPS.
claims.quote: All network data security integrations support classifying traffic sent and received from an endpoint device over HTTP and HTTPS protocols to websites, cloud apps, and generative AI services.

claims.claim: WebSocket support can differ by integrated solution.
claims.quote: Support for WebSocket protocol may differ depending on the integrated SASE or non-Microsoft secure browser solution. Check with your solution provider for details on supported protocols.

claims.claim: The general integration entry point is Microsoft Purview portal > Data Loss Prevention > Security Store > Get solution.
claims.quote: Open the Data Loss Prevention solution and select Security Store from the left navigation bar. Select Get solution for the provider you're using.

claims.claim: No automation for enabling the Prisma Access Security Store integration is documented in the references found.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview Prisma Access Security Store integration API PowerShell; site:learn.microsoft.com "Purview" "Security Store" "PowerShell" "integration". Opened network overview and DLP and collection setup pages; they document portal and provider setup, not an enablement API.

claims.claim: The DLP creation entry point is Microsoft Purview portal > Data loss prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Inline web traffic.
claims.quote: Select Data loss prevention > Policies > + Create policy. Select Inline web traffic.
claims.fix: Add to controls[1].note: 'The cited Learn scenario notes that some features used are in preview.' Preserve the existing statement that these are general network data security controls.

claims.claim: Security & Compliance PowerShell documents New-DlpCompliancePolicy -Name <policy name> -EnforcementPlanes @("Network") for creating a DLP policy with the Network enforcement plane.
claims.quote: The EnforcementPlanes parameter defines the layer where policy actions are run. ... -EnforcementPlanes @("<Value>"). Valid values are: ... Network

claims.claim: The DLP cmdlet reference has no network-specific example.
claims.quote: Searched: Network and Examples in the full New-DlpCompliancePolicy reference. Read Examples 1-4: SharePoint, SharePoint/OneDrive, Power BI and Copilot. Network appears as a valid EnforcementPlanes value but not in an example.

claims.claim: Collection policy creation starts at Microsoft Purview portal > Data loss prevention > Classifiers > Collection policies > + Create policy.
claims.quote: Open the Data loss prevention solution and navigate to Classifiers > Collection policies. Select + Create policy.

claims.claim: No documented automation specifically creating network collection policies was found.
claims.quote: Searched: "collection" "Network" "New-FeatureConfiguration"; "Purview" "collection policies" "Graph" "create" network. Read New-FeatureConfiguration in full: examples cover Copilot, Browser and Devices, with no Network configuration; network setup page gives portal steps.

claims.claim: The Learn policy scenarios enable Network and non-Microsoft secure browsers as an enforcement location.
claims.quote: Ensure Network and non-Microsoft secure browsers is enabled and select Next.

claims.claim: DLP Compliance Management is a listed collection-policy role.
claims.quote: Here's a list of applicable roles. DLP Compliance Management

claims.claim: Organization Management is a listed applicable role group.
claims.quote: Here's a list of applicable role groups. Organization Management

claims.claim: Compliance Administrator is a listed applicable role group.
claims.quote: Compliance Administrator

claims.claim: Insider Risk Management Admin is a listed applicable role group.
claims.quote: Insider Risk Management Admin

claims.claim: Information Protection Admins is a listed applicable role group.
claims.quote: Information Protection Admins

claims.claim: Data Security Viewers is listed for read-only support.
claims.quote: Data Security Viewers (read-only support)

claims.claim: Activity explorer supports the Enforcement plane filter set to Network.
claims.quote: Select + Add filter and choose Enforcement plane. Click the Enforcement plane filter and select Network. Select Apply.

claims.claim: DSPM reports can show interactions detected by network collection policies.
claims.quote: Navigate to Reports to see high level reports and graphs breaking down the interactions detected by the collection policy.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout and After rollout
claims.claim: Network data security matches are available in activity explorer and DLP alerts when alerts are configured.
claims.quote: Data from network data security appear in activity explorer, Data Security Posture Management activity explorer events, and if alerts are enabled, DLP alerts.

claims.claim: Existing Purview policies and reporting can be used for Prisma Access data rather than rebuilding governance in another tool.
claims.quote: Existing Purview DLP and network data security policies can be applied to network-based data flows through Palo Alto Prisma Access.

claims.claim: Administrators configure the integration in Security Store, then define conditions, activities and cloud apps in collection or DLP policies; collection is for discovery rather than enforcement.
claims.quote: extending discovery and protection to the network layer through collection policies for data discovery, data loss prevention policies for protection, or both, depending on your organization's needs.

claims.claim: The network data security page links to Purview billing models for pay-as-you-go pricing information.
claims.quote: For more information on pay-as-you-go billing for network data security, see Other Microsoft Purview solutions that use pay-as-you-go pricing and Requests.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout and After rollout; controls
claims.claim: The checklist tells administrators to check billing configuration and usage, activity explorer, DSPM reports and DLP alerts without corresponding control rows.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'Confirm Purview pay-as-you-go billing is configured'; 'Filter activity explorer'; 'check DSPM reports'; 'Check DLP alerts and billing usage'. Table rows cover only integration enablement, DLP policy creation and collection policy creation.
claims.fix: The billing configuration/usage, activity explorer filter, DSPM reporting and DLP alert checks have no rows. Remove those checklist instructions to meet the table/checklist rule without adding unverified controls; retain their factual explanations elsewhere.

claims.claim: No separate tenant switch beyond enabling the integration in Security Store is described.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview Prisma Access Security Store integration API PowerShell; "Palo Alto" "Prisma Access" "Purview". Read MC1257999, the network overview and both setup scenarios; these describe Security Store integration enablement, not an additional tenant switch.
